title: Article 124 — Establishment and constitution of Supreme Court

content.overview: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court of India, consisting of a Chief Justice of India and, until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number, other Judges. Judges are appointed by the President after consultation with such of the Judges of the Supreme Court and of the High Courts as the President may deem necessary (the Chief Justice of India is always consulted for appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice). A Judge holds office until age 65, may resign to the President, and may be removed only by the process in Article 124(4)–(5) (address by each House on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity). Qualifications and oath are also provided.
content.glance: SC: CJI + other Judges (number by Parliament). Appointment by President after consultation (collegium practice). Tenure to 65; removal only by parliamentary address for proved misbehaviour/incapacity.
content.study:
Article 124:
(1) There shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice of India and, until Parliament by law prescribes a larger number, of not more than [prescribed number] other Judges.
(2) Every Judge of the Supreme Court shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal after consultation with such of the Judges of the Supreme Court and of the High Courts in the States as the President may deem necessary for the purpose and shall hold office until he attains the age of sixty-five years:
Provided that in the case of appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of India shall always be consulted.
…
(4)–(5) Removal: only by order of the President after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity; procedure regulated by parliamentary law.

Appointment practice has been shaped by the collegium judgments (Second Judges, Third Judges, and the NJAC decision striking down the 99th Amendment / Arts 124A–C). Arts 124A–C (NJAC) were inserted by the 99th Amendment and struck down; they are treated as inoperative (P0).

Examination: establishment; composition; appointment (President + consultation / collegium); age 65; removal only by special parliamentary address for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

sections.heading: Establishment and appointment
sections.body:
1. Supreme Court: CJI + other Judges (number prescribed by Parliament by law).
2. Appointment: President by warrant after consultation; CJI always consulted for non-CJI appointments.
3. Tenure: until age 65; resignation to President.
4. Removal: only under Art 124(4)–(5) — address by each House (special majorities) for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

sections.heading: NJAC note
sections.body: Articles 124A–124C (National Judicial Appointments Commission) inserted by the 99th Amendment were struck down by the Supreme Court and are inoperative.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the establishment and appointment of Supreme Court Judges under Article 124.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court of India consisting of the Chief Justice of India and other Judges (number as Parliament by law prescribes). Judges are appointed by the President after consultation with such Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts as the President deems necessary; the Chief Justice of India is always consulted for appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice. A Judge holds office until the age of 65 and may be removed only by the President after an address by each House of Parliament on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, supported by the special majorities specified in Article 124(4).
